support: Neve brought her class to watch that last reading, the last time anyone would cross the lawn to the box.
The box still stands on the lawn with its door latched, and at nine each morning the children walk past it on their way into school.
WV9-P01.5.note: The closing images of a last reading, an empty page and a latched box are wistful; admiring is also defensible because the passage dwells on Ida's forty-one years with only one gap and her own idea of the sensor.

support: The contractor, Joss Hebden, came to the next walk himself, on his knees at the steep strip with a red torch like everyone else.
He has moved the mowing back to September, paid to reseed the bare banks out of his own pocket, and asked Rowe for a copy of her map, which he now keeps in his van.
WV9-P02.5.note: Read literally, the contractor coming himself, reseeding at his own cost and keeping the map shows admiration; the details 'on his knees ... like everyone else' and the map 'now keeps in his van' can be read as dry and gently amused, so A is defensible.
